Change c0549. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): I shall no longer see the sun or stars, or feel the winds play on my cheeks.

1818 text: Light, feeling, and sense, will pass away; and in this condition must I find my happiness. Some years ago, when the images which this world affords first opened upon me, when I felt the cheering warmth of summer, and heard the rustling of the leaves and the chirping of the birds, and these were all to me, I should have wept to die; now it is my only consolation.

1831 text: Light, feeling, and sense will pass away; and in this condition must I find my happiness. Some years ago, when the images which this world affords first opened upon me, when I felt the cheering warmth of summer, and heard the rustling of the leaves and the warbling of the birds, and these were all to me, I should have wept to die; now it is my only consolation.

Diff: Light, feeling, and sense [-,-] will pass away; and in this condition must I find my happiness. Some years ago, when the images which this world affords first opened upon me, when I felt the cheering warmth of summer, and heard the rustling of the leaves and the [-chirping-] {+warbling+} of the birds, and these were all to me, I should have wept to die; now it is my only consolation.

Context after (unchanged): Polluted by crimes, and torn by the bitterest remorse, where can I find rest but in death?

result.rationale: Only 'chirping' is replaced by 'warbling' for the birds' song; the meaning and the narrator's sensory memory are unchanged. The comma removal after 'sense' is punctuation-level and similarly inconsequential.
